result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_assortativity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate assortativity for numeric node attributes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23738-L23821){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_assortativity(attribute) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Measures the tendency of nodes with similar numeric attribute values to connect. Returns the Pearson correlation coefficient of attribute values across edges, indicating whether similar values tend to be connected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attribute]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the numeric node attribute to analyze. Must exist on all nodes and be convertible to float. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Assortativity coefficient in range `[-1, 1]`: - `r = 1`: perfect positive correlation (identical values connect) - `r > 0`: assortative (similar values prefer to connect) - `r = 0`: no correlation - `r < 0`: disassortative (dissimilar values prefer to connect) - `r = -1`: perfect negative correlation ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If attribute doesn't exist on all nodes, isn't numeric, graph has no edges, or attribute has no variance. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - uses Pearson correlation coefficient formula - common in social networks (homophily by age, income, education) - can reveal hierarchical structures when negative - sensitive to outliers: considers data normalization - requires variance in attribute values (all same value will error) ## Examples {.doc-examples} When people mostly befriend others close to their own age, connecting similar numeric values, the numeric assortativity comes out positive: ::: {#6826f2ed .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node("Alice", age=25) .add_node("Bob", age=27) .add_node("Carol", age=26) .add_node("Dave", age=55) .add_node("Eve", age=53) .add_edge("Alice", "Bob") # Similar ages (25-27) .add_edge("Bob", "Carol") # Similar ages (27-26) .add_edge("Dave", "Eve") # Similar ages (55-53) .add_edge("Alice", "Carol") # Similar ages (25-26) ) # Returns a positive value: similar-aged people tend to connect g.get_assortativity("age") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.9915397631133672 ``` ::: ::: In academic mentorship networks, senior researchers often collaborate with junior ones, connecting dissimilar values and producing a negative coefficient: ::: {#4c2f365d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node("Junior1", papers=5) .add_node("Junior2", papers=7) .add_node("Senior1", papers=50) .add_node("Senior2", papers=45) .add_edge("Senior1", "Junior1") .add_edge("Senior1", "Junior2") .add_edge("Senior2", "Junior1") ) # Returns a negative value: experienced researchers connect to juniors g.get_assortativity("papers") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` -0.9905454545454547 ``` ::: :::
